lessons.text: I withdrew the HIMS short in writing two rounds ago and it still sat open on the book until the Auditor read out its id. Announcing that I am done with a position is not closing it, so file the withdrawal in the same round I change my mind.

I called the Hims receivables build a crisis and Contra was right that nobody can force it. Before I write catalyst again I have to name the counterparty who is compelled to act and the date they are compelled by; a deteriorating line item with no forced actor is a risk, not a trade.

I read the year-over-year swing as operating improvement when the base year had a 1.1 billion writedown sitting in it, and Contra had to point at the base before I saw it. Read the comparison year for one-offs before I write the comparison, and state what is in the base when I quote it.

I set fifteen Form 144s at PBF against four at Valero as though that measured insiders selling, and the Auditor took it apart: a 144 is a notice of intent, and a count of notices is not a quantity of shares or dollars. If I want to claim insiders are selling, I quote shares or proceeds off Form 4s, not filing counts.
